Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Tellus Tech (POC + procurement)

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the discussion today — really appreciate the context on Tellus Tech's roadmap and the challenges you outlined. Below is a short recap (pain, current stack, success criteria) and then a procurement framing so we can align next steps.

Recap — Pain & goals
- Latency and cost variability on customer-facing summarization flows (peak 80 RPS during batch windows).
- Need predictable per-token costs and a fallback strategy when load spikes.
- Security: audit logs, encryption at rest, and SOC2 evidence required for vendor onboarding.

Current stack
- Primary frontend: React + Node.js
- Back end: Kubernetes on GCP (us-west1) with GPUs for training, inference currently via managed API provider + in-house caching layer
- Auth: Okta SSO, product data stored in GCP (no PII persisted to vendor endpoints)

Success criteria for POC
1) 95th pct latency under 400ms for 512-token responses in your staging traffic profile
2) Monthly E2E cost predictability within 15% of baseline for target throughput
3) Integration with Okta SSO and access to audit logs for an initial 30-day retention window

Procurement framing & next steps
- Decision process: you indicated procurement + legal + platform engineering will review. Typical timeline you mentioned: internal exec review in mid-Dec; procurement/PO by end of December.
- Stakeholders to involve: Liam O'Connor (Product), Rachel Singh (Procurement), Mark Lawson (Security/InfoSec), and Legal (we can loop in if you provide the contact).
- Initial commercial guardrails (ballpark): for a 3-month POC with dedicated support and scoped token limits, you should expect pricing in the ~$50k–$120k range depending on model/throughput choices. We will tighten this after we size the POC and agree on SLA requirements.
- Deliverables from Redwood: draft SOW for the POC, SOC2 summary (attached), and a one-page PO/contract checklist for your procurement team.

Attachments: Redwood_POC_SOW_v1.pdf (draft SOW), SOC2-summary.xlsx

Requested next actions
1) Please confirm the stakeholders & expected decision owner and target decision date.
2) Are there specific security artifacts we should prioritize (e.g., penetration test report, specific KMS/HSM requirements)?
3) If agreeable, let's schedule a 30-minute procurement sync next week to walk through the SOW and PO checklist (I penciled in Wed 12/2 and Thu 12/3 — let me know what works).

I'll get Rishi and Vivek aligned on a compact SOW and an initial commercial ballpark that maps to the POC scope.

Thanks,

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap, that aligns with my notes. A few quick answers / details from our side:

Stakeholders & contacts
- Decision owner: Me (Product) + final sign-off by VP Ops (Amina Patel).
- Procurement: Rachel Singh (procurement@tellus-tech.com) — copied.
- Legal: legal@tellus-tech.com — copied.
- Security: Mark Lawson (mark.lawson@tellus-tech.com) — will add him on follow-ups.

Timeline
- Exec review: target week of Dec 14 for go/no-go on POC funding.
- Procurement/PO: target before Dec 31 if exec approves.

Security artifacts
- SOC2 report & penetration test summary would be ideal. KMS integration is required (we use Google KMS today) and we need confirmation that keys can be customer-managed or that there are clear encryption-at-rest guarantees.

Commercial guardrails (helpful)
- Budget expectations: to be conservative, our finance team is looking at ~100k USD for the POC line item; flexibility exists but they'd like a 1) upper bound cap and 2) a clear overage policy.

Next steps
- Please send the draft SOW and a one-pager procurement checklist; we'll route to Rachel + Legal.
- Wed 12/2 at 11:00 PT works for a procurement sync for me — Rachel, can you confirm?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Liam
